correctness.rationale: The square-multiplier affine group sends ordered differences in the square and nonsquare cosets to 1 and 3, respectively. An independent re-enumeration (independent_puncture_check.py) checked no 4-cliques, 136 edge-preserving affine maps and both full pair orbits. Using the supplied trees as data, a separately written triangle-first relator elimination after tree contraction exhausts every non-tree edge. Inductively each chosen triangle forces its one remaining generator to be trivial. For the ambient, single, adjacent-pair and nonadjacent-pair cases the numbers of remaining triangles are 16, 11, 8 and 6; the last two face vectors are (15,53,47) and (15,52,44). The frozen script actually orders by (unresolved edge, triangle), not triangle first as the text says; the independent triangle-first check also succeeds. In dimension two H₂ is free and Euler characteristic determines its rank once π₁ is trivial. Hurewicz followed by the homology form of Whitehead gives the indicated sphere wedges. For the actual inclusion, H₃(K,D)=0 and H₂(K,D) is a subgroup of the free relative two-chain group; H₁(D)=0 makes it the cokernel of the injected H₂(D). Thus the cokernel is free of rank 16−8 or 16−6 and the inclusion splits integrally. The optional intermediate link calculation was also checked: vertex/edge/cycle-rank triples (8,12,5), (7,9,3), (8,12,5). The frozen verifier was inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: This is a complete two-point loss profile on a canonical conference and Ramsey graph, where symmetry gives exactly two natural erasure types. It tells a researcher which type retains more two-dimensional topology, and that neither introduces one-dimensional topology or a nonprimitive second-homology image. Neither an Euler check alone nor the ambient sphere count answers that question. Scope is exactly this graph and two induced deletions.
